description: Banco oficial de mini-diálogos guiados multi-turno para las rutas A1-C2 de Conversation. Cada ítem plantea una conversación dirigida: un contexto, el rol del alumno, el rol del tutor (que interpreta al otro hablante siguiendo la situación), una línea de apertura y unas metas comunicativas que el alumno debe cumplir conversando varios turnos. Al terminar, se evalúa el transcripto completo con el pipeline LLM de evidencia (task_type conversation) fusionado con la señal objetiva de interacción. Alineado con los can_do y el léxico de backend/curriculum/<level>.json.

items.context: You arrive at your first English lesson and sit next to a student you do not know.
items.student_role: A new student in an English class.
items.tutor_role: A friendly classmate sitting next to you.
items.opening_line: Hi! I am Tom. What is your name?
communicative_goals: Say hello and give your name
Say where you are from
Ask his name again politely if you do not hear it

items.context: You meet your neighbour in the lift one morning.
items.student_role: A neighbour going to work.
items.opening_line: Good morning! How are you today?
communicative_goals: Greet him and answer 'How are you?'
Ask how he is
Say goodbye politely when you leave

items.context: It is your first day at a language school and you need a few things for the lesson.
items.student_role: A new student.
items.tutor_role: The teacher, who wants to help you.
items.opening_line: Hello! Welcome. Do you have everything for today's lesson?
communicative_goals: Ask politely for a pen and a notebook
Answer if the teacher asks if you have your book
Say thank you

items.context: You are at a small café and you want something to eat and drink.
items.student_role: A customer at a café.
items.opening_line: Good afternoon. What would you like?
communicative_goals: Order a drink and something to eat
Ask how much it is
Say thank you

items.context: You are in a clothes shop and you want to buy a T-shirt.
items.student_role: A customer.
items.opening_line: Hello! Can I help you?
communicative_goals: Say what you want to buy
Ask the price
Say if you want it or not

items.context: A new friend asks you about your family.
items.student_role: You, talking about your family.
items.opening_line: Do you have a big family?
communicative_goals: Answer about your brothers and sisters
Say something about one person in your family
Ask about his or her family

items.context: Your teacher wants to know about your English class times.
items.student_role: A student.
items.opening_line: What time is your English class?
communicative_goals: Say the time of your English class
Say what day you have class
Ask what time the next class is

items.context: A friend phones you before going out and talks about the weather.
items.student_role: You, ready to go out.
items.opening_line: It is very cold today, is not it?
communicative_goals: Agree or disagree about the weather
Say what you wear when it is cold
Ask what the weather is like tomorrow

items.context: You and a classmate are talking about the food you like.
items.student_role: A student talking about food.
items.opening_line: Do you like pizza?
communicative_goals: Say yes or no
Name one food you like and one you do not like
Ask what food your classmate likes

items.context: A classmate asks what you do every day.
items.student_role: A student describing their daily routine.
items.opening_line: What do you do every morning?
communicative_goals: Say two things you do every day
Say what time you get up
Ask what your classmate does on Sunday

items.context: You are in a new building and you cannot find the bathroom.
items.student_role: A visitor in a new building.
items.opening_line: Hello. Do you need any help?
communicative_goals: Ask where the bathroom is
Answer when he asks if it is your first day
Say thank you

items.context: You want to buy a jacket but you are not sure about the size and colour.
items.student_role: A customer in a clothes shop.
items.opening_line: Good morning! Are you looking for something special?
communicative_goals: Say you are looking for a jacket and ask your size
Ask to try it on
Ask about the price and if you can pay by card

items.context: You are having lunch in a restaurant, but your dish is not what you ordered.
items.student_role: A customer at a restaurant.
items.opening_line: Here you are. Enjoy your meal!
communicative_goals: Explain politely that this is not what you ordered
Say what dish you actually ordered
Thank the waiter when he fixes the problem

items.context: You are in a new city and you need to get to the train station.
items.student_role: A visitor asking for directions.
items.opening_line: Excuse me, are you looking for something?
communicative_goals: Ask how to get to the train station
Ask if it is far and how long it takes
Repeat the instructions to confirm you understood

items.context: You want to invite a friend to the cinema this weekend.
items.student_role: You, making a plan with a friend.
items.tutor_role: A friend who is not sure yet.
items.opening_line: Hi! Are you doing anything this weekend?
communicative_goals: Invite your friend to the cinema
Suggest a day and a time
Agree on the plan when your friend answers

items.context: You are back from a short holiday and a colleague asks about it.
items.student_role: You, telling someone about your holiday.
items.opening_line: How was your holiday? Did you have a good time?
communicative_goals: Say where you went and who you went with
Say two things you did there
Answer follow-up questions about the weather or the food

items.context: You are phoning a small hotel to book a room for two nights.
items.student_role: A guest booking a room by phone.
items.opening_line: Good morning, City Hotel. How can I help you?
communicative_goals: Say you want a single room for two nights
Ask the price per night and if breakfast is included
Confirm your name and the dates

items.context: You left your bag on the bus this morning and you are asking at the lost property office.
items.student_role: A passenger who lost a bag.
items.opening_line: Good afternoon. Can I help you?
communicative_goals: Explain that you lost your bag on the bus
Describe the bag and what is inside
Ask when and how you can collect it

items.context: You have a sore throat and a headache, and you go to the pharmacy.
items.student_role: A customer at the pharmacy.
items.opening_line: Hello. What can I do for you?
communicative_goals: Describe your problem simply
Ask for something for a sore throat
Answer questions about how long you have felt ill

items.context: A friend invites you to her birthday party next Saturday.
items.student_role: A friend who is invited to a party.
items.tutor_role: The friend who is organising the party.
items.opening_line: I am having a birthday party next Saturday. Would you like to come?
communicative_goals: Accept the invitation happily
Ask what time the party starts and where it is
Ask if you should bring anything

items.context: You are talking to a friend about two cities you both know.
items.student_role: You, comparing two cities.
items.tutor_role: A friend with a different opinion.
items.opening_line: I think Barcelona is nicer than Madrid, is not it?
communicative_goals: Give your opinion about the two cities
Compare them using words like bigger, cheaper or busier
Agree or disagree politely with your friend

items.context: A classmate asks you about how often you do things in your daily life.
items.student_role: A student talking about habits.
items.opening_line: How often do you go to the supermarket?
communicative_goals: Answer using words like always, usually or never
Say what you do at the weekend
Ask your classmate about one of his or her habits

items.context: You have a dentist appointment tomorrow but you cannot go, so you call to change it.
items.student_role: A patient calling the dentist's office.
items.tutor_role: The receptionist at the dentist's office.
items.opening_line: Good morning, Green Dental Clinic. How can I help you?
communicative_goals: Explain that you need to change your appointment and why
Suggest a new day and time that works for you
Confirm the new appointment details before ending the call

items.context: The headphones you bought last week stopped working. You are back at the shop.
items.student_role: A customer returning a faulty product.
items.opening_line: Hello. Is everything okay with your headphones?
communicative_goals: Explain the problem with the headphones
Say when you bought them and show that you have the receipt
Ask for a replacement or a refund and respond to the assistant's offer

items.context: You are at a tourist information office planning a day trip for tomorrow.
items.student_role: A tourist asking for information.
items.opening_line: Good morning! What would you like to know?
communicative_goals: Ask about the best way to visit the old town
Ask about opening times and ticket prices
Ask for a recommendation for somewhere to eat nearby

items.context: You have been feeling tired all week and you are at the doctor's surgery.
items.student_role: A patient at the doctor's.
items.opening_line: Come in and sit down. So, what can I do for you?
communicative_goals: Describe how you have been feeling and for how long
Answer the doctor's questions about your sleep and routine
Ask what you should do and repeat the advice to confirm you understood

items.context: You and a friend are planning a three-day trip together and need to decide some things.
items.student_role: You, planning a trip with a friend.
items.tutor_role: A friend who has some ideas.
items.opening_line: So, where should we stay for the trip?
communicative_goals: Give your opinion about where to stay
Make a suggestion about what to do one of the days
Reach an agreement with your friend about the plan

items.context: Your teacher gives you homework instructions, but you did not understand part of them.
items.student_role: A student in a language class.
items.opening_line: Any questions about the homework?
communicative_goals: Ask the teacher to repeat the part you did not understand
Paraphrase what you understood to check it is right
Ask for an example of what you have to do

items.topic: Small talk at a work event
items.context: You are at a company party and you start talking to a colleague from another department.
items.student_role: An employee making small talk.
items.tutor_role: A colleague you have not met before.
items.opening_line: Hi! Are you enjoying the party?
communicative_goals: Answer and ask what department he or she works in
Talk a little about what you do at work
Find something you both have in common

items.context: You are viewing a small flat and you ask the landlord some questions before deciding.
items.student_role: Someone looking for a flat to rent.
items.tutor_role: The landlord showing you the flat.
items.opening_line: So, what do you think of the flat so far?
communicative_goals: Give your first impression of the flat
Ask about the monthly rent and bills
Ask about the neighbours or the area and when you could move in

items.context: A friend asks you to recommend a film to watch tonight.
items.student_role: You, recommending a film.
items.tutor_role: A friend who wants a recommendation.
items.opening_line: I cannot decide what to watch tonight. Any ideas?
communicative_goals: Recommend a film you enjoyed
Explain why it is good and what it is about
Answer your friend's questions about the film

items.context: You have just joined a gym and you want to know how things work there.
items.student_role: A new gym member.
items.tutor_role: A member of staff at the gym.
items.opening_line: Welcome to the gym! Do you have any questions?
communicative_goals: Ask about the opening hours at the weekend
Ask if you can bring a guest
Ask about the rules for canceling your membership

items.context: It is your first week in a new job and you need some help from a colleague.
items.student_role: A new employee.
items.tutor_role: A colleague who is happy to help.
items.opening_line: Hi! How is your first week going?
communicative_goals: Say how your first week is going and mention one difficulty
Ask a practical question about how the office works
Thank the colleague and ask who else you should talk to

items.context: Your internet has been down for three days and you are talking to a customer service manager after several calls.
items.student_role: A customer who has had a serious problem.
items.opening_line: I understand you have had some trouble with your service. Tell me what happened.
communicative_goals: Explain the situation clearly, including how long the problem has lasted
Describe the impact the problem has had on you
Propose a fair solution and confirm what the manager offers

items.context: A colleague thinks working from the office is better than working from home. You disagree.
items.student_role: You, defending your point of view.
items.tutor_role: A colleague with a different opinion.
items.opening_line: Honestly, I think working from the office is much more productive.
communicative_goals: Give your opinion with two clear reasons
Respond to your colleague's arguments without repeating yourself
Concede one good point and keep the discussion constructive

items.context: Your project manager wants the report by Friday, but you think that is unrealistic.
items.student_role: An employee who needs more time.
items.opening_line: So, can we count on the full report by Friday?
communicative_goals: Explain honestly why Friday is difficult
Propose a realistic alternative with reasons
Reach an agreement that both of you accept

items.context: You are in a job interview for a position that interests you a lot.
items.student_role: A candidate in a job interview.
items.opening_line: Tell me a little about yourself and why you applied for this role.
communicative_goals: Introduce yourself and explain why you are interested in the role
Describe one relevant experience and what you learned from it
Answer a question about your weaknesses honestly and positively

items.context: You are at the bank asking about opening an account and getting a small credit card.
items.student_role: A customer at the bank.
items.opening_line: Good morning. What can we help you with today?
communicative_goals: Explain that you want to open an account
Ask about the conditions and monthly fees
Ask what documents you need to bring

items.context: You and a friend are planning a two-week trip and disagree about how many cities to visit.
items.student_role: You, planning a trip with a friend.
items.tutor_role: A friend who wants to visit many places quickly.
items.opening_line: I think we should visit five cities in two weeks. That sounds exciting!
communicative_goals: Explain why travelling too quickly can be a problem
Suggest an itinerary that balances sightseeing and rest
Persuade your friend to try your approach

items.context: You are on the phone with IT support because your laptop will not start after an update.
items.student_role: An employee with a technical problem.
items.opening_line: Thanks for waiting. Can you describe exactly what happens when you turn it on?
communicative_goals: Describe the problem step by step
Answer the technician's questions about what you tried
Follow the instructions and confirm whether the problem is solved

items.context: In a team meeting, a colleague proposes an idea that you think has a serious weakness.
items.student_role: A team member in a meeting.
items.tutor_role: A colleague who proposed the idea.
items.opening_line: I really believe this new idea will save us time and money.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge the strengths of the idea first
Raise your concern politely and explain why it matters
Suggest how the idea could be improved so the team can move forward

items.context: You love a flat but the rent is higher than you wanted to pay.
items.student_role: A person negotiating the rent of a flat.
items.opening_line: So, are you interested in renting the flat?
communicative_goals: Say you like the flat but the rent is too high for you
Propose a lower price and justify it
Negotiate until you reach an arrangement both can accept

items.context: You are discussing with a friend whether the city should close its centre to private cars.
items.student_role: You, defending your position in a debate.
items.tutor_role: A friend with strong arguments on the other side.
items.opening_line: Closing the centre to cars would be terrible for the shops.
communicative_goals: State your position clearly with reasons
Challenge one of your friend's arguments with a counterexample
Use a conditional structure to describe the consequences of each option

items.context: A friend is hesitating about signing up for a charity run with you.
items.student_role: You, persuading a friend to join you.
items.tutor_role: A friend who is not sure.
items.opening_line: I signed us up for the charity run. You are coming too, right?
communicative_goals: Explain why the run is a good idea and who it helps
Address your friend's worries about fitness or time
Offer practical help so your friend feels ready to join

items.context: In an academic tutorial, your tutor challenges one of the conclusions of your essay.
items.student_role: A student discussing their essay.
items.opening_line: Your conclusion is interesting, but do you think your evidence really supports it?
communicative_goals: Defend your conclusion while acknowledging its limitations
Clarify which evidence is strongest and why
Engage with the tutor's counterargument and refine your position

items.context: A client is asking for extra work that was not in the contract, within the original deadline.
items.student_role: A professional managing a client relationship.
items.tutor_role: A client who wants more than was agreed.
items.opening_line: We need you to add these three features by the same date. That should not be a problem, right?
communicative_goals: Explain the impact of the new request on the agreed scope
Propose a realistic alternative, such as a revised date or a phased delivery
Protect the relationship while keeping the agreement sustainable

items.context: At a dinner party, someone argues that social media does more harm than good to society.
items.student_role: You, participating in a nuanced debate.
items.tutor_role: A guest with strong opinions on social media.
items.opening_line: I honestly think social media has destroyed real conversation.
communicative_goals: Give a balanced response that acknowledges both harms and benefits
Introduce a distinction that reframes the discussion
Challenge an overgeneralisation politely and keep the tone respectful

items.context: You have to explain how your company's recommendation system works to a non-technical audience.
items.student_role: An expert explaining a technical concept.
items.tutor_role: An intelligent listener without technical background.
items.opening_line: I have heard your system uses artificial intelligence. How does it actually decide what to show me?
communicative_goals: Explain the concept using a clear analogy
Simplify technical terms without losing accuracy
Check that the listener has understood and answer follow-up questions

items.context: You need to give constructive feedback to a colleague whose recent presentation was disorganised.
items.student_role: A senior colleague giving feedback.
items.tutor_role: A colleague who feels defensive about their work.
items.opening_line: So, what did you think of my presentation the other day?
communicative_goals: Start with what worked well and be specific
Raise the area that needs improvement without causing defensiveness
Agree with your colleague on one concrete action for next time

items.context: You are leading a retrospective after a project that finished late, and the team is blaming each other.
items.student_role: The team lead running the retrospective.
items.opening_line: I just want to say, the delay was not our fault. The requirements kept changing.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge the frustration and steer the conversation away from blame
Ask questions that focus on process rather than people
Summarise the discussion into two concrete actions for the next project

items.context: An external partner is unhappy about the quality of a recent delivery and is threatening to end the contract.
items.student_role: A manager responding to a partner's concerns.
items.opening_line: Frankly, we are not satisfied. This delivery was below the standard we agreed on.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge the concern without admitting fault prematurely
Ask clarifying questions to understand the specific problem
Propose a concrete recovery plan and agree on how to verify it

items.context: You want your manager to invest in a new training programme for your team, but the budget is tight.
items.student_role: An employee presenting a business case.
items.tutor_role: A cautious manager who controls the budget.
items.opening_line: I have seen your proposal for training. The problem is the budget this year.
communicative_goals: Present the long-term value of the investment with concrete examples
Anticipate the manager's objections and respond to them
Offer a compromise, such as a pilot programme, to get approval

items.context: At the end of a long meeting, you want to make sure everyone agrees on what was decided.
items.student_role: A participant summarising the meeting.
items.tutor_role: A colleague who is not sure the summary is accurate.
items.opening_line: I am not sure we all left the meeting with the same understanding.
communicative_goals: Summarise the key decisions in your own words
Identify one point where there is still ambiguity
Propose who does what and by when, and confirm agreement

items.context: A colleague suggests presenting some reused work as new to impress a client.
items.student_role: You, handling an ethical dilemma with tact.
items.tutor_role: A colleague suggesting a questionable shortcut.
items.opening_line: Listen, we could easily present last year's framework as a new solution. Nobody would know.
communicative_goals: Express your discomfort without accusing your colleague
Explain the risks of the shortcut for the client and the team
Suggest an honest alternative that still meets the client's needs

items.context: A friend is convinced by a persuasive online article that you think is misleading.
items.student_role: You, discussing media critically.
items.tutor_role: A friend who trusts the article completely.
items.opening_line: Have you seen this article? It explains everything perfectly. It must be true.
communicative_goals: Question the article's reliability without dismissing your friend
Point out specific techniques of persuasion it uses
Suggest how your friend could verify the claims themselves

items.context: You are in the final round of negotiating a commercial contract, and one clause is still blocking the agreement.
items.student_role: A senior negotiator.
items.tutor_role: A counterpart who is equally skilled at negotiating.
items.opening_line: We cannot accept clause 14 as it stands. It exposes us to unlimited liability.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge the concern and separate the issue from the relationship
Propose a reformulation of the clause that protects both parties
Trade concessions deliberately and reach a balanced final agreement

items.context: In a viva or public defence, an examiner questions the theoretical foundation of your work.
items.student_role: A researcher defending their thesis.
items.opening_line: Your framework rests on an assumption that, frankly, many in the field would contest.
communicative_goals: Restate the examiner's objection precisely to show you understood it
Defend the assumption while acknowledging its scope and limits
Situate your contribution within the broader scholarly debate

items.context: You are chairing a meeting between two departments that have reached a public impasse over priorities.
items.student_role: The chair of a difficult meeting.
items.tutor_role: A department head who is unwilling to compromise.
items.opening_line: I will be direct: my department will not postpone our release for your project.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge each side's legitimate constraints
Reframe the conflict around shared organisational goals
Guide the participants toward a concrete compromise they can both claim as a win

items.context: A talented junior colleague is struggling with a difficult client and asks for your advice.
items.student_role: A senior professional coaching a colleague.
items.tutor_role: A junior colleague who is losing confidence.
items.opening_line: To be honest, that client makes me anxious and I do not know how to handle the last conversation.
communicative_goals: Help the colleague reframe the situation without minimising their feelings
Ask questions that lead them to their own solution
Agree on concrete next steps and a way to review progress

items.context: A colleague publishes a report full of impressive data, and you suspect the conclusions overreach.
items.student_role: A peer offering a critical analysis.
items.opening_line: I would love your feedback on my report before I send it to the board.
communicative_goals: Praise what is genuinely strong in the report
Question the link between the data and the conclusions with precision
Suggest how the analysis could be made more rigorous while preserving its impact

items.context: During an international call, a partner makes an ambiguous comment that could be an accusation or a joke.
items.student_role: A professional navigating ambiguity diplomatically.
items.opening_line: Of course, we all know how these things tend to go in your country, do we not?
communicative_goals: Respond without assuming bad faith or confirming the stereotype
Ask a clarifying question that invites the partner to be explicit
Redirect the conversation toward the shared objective tactfully

items.context: After giving a keynote address, you face a difficult question from the audience about a sensitive statistic.
items.student_role: A speaker fielding questions.
items.opening_line: Your statistic about unemployment seems to contradict what the government published last month.
communicative_goals: Thank the questioner and validate the quality of the question
Clarify the methodological difference behind the two figures
Concede uncertainty where it exists and offer to share sources

items.context: In a strategy meeting, a consultant presents an elegant analysis whose recommendation you find risky.
items.student_role: A senior decision-maker challenging a recommendation.
items.opening_line: Our recommendation is clear: enter the new market this year. The analysis leaves little room for doubt.
communicative_goals: Acknowledge the elegance of the analysis and its strengths
Probe the assumptions that, if wrong, would change the recommendation
Press for a clear account of the downside risk before a decision is taken

items.context: A close friend in a position of power offers you an advantage that crosses an ethical line, framed as a favour.
items.student_role: You, navigating a personal ethical dilemma.
items.tutor_role: A friend who does not see the problem.
items.opening_line: Do not worry, I will make sure you get the contract. Consider it a favour between friends.
communicative_goals: Make clear the boundary without destroying the friendship
Explain the consequences for both of you if the favour became known
Offer an honest way forward that protects your integrity

items.context: A peer from another discipline asks you to explain a subtle technical concept in your field that affects their work.
items.student_role: An expert consulted by a peer.
items.tutor_role: A brilliant peer from another field.
items.opening_line: I have read your papers, but I need to understand the practical implications of your model for my research.
communicative_goals: Explain the concept at the level of precision your peer needs
Draw the connections to your peer's field to make the implications concrete
Probe your peer's assumptions to sharpen the shared understanding

items.context: A cultural misunderstanding has made a new colleague think you were rude in a meeting. You want to repair it.
items.student_role: You, repairing a cross-cultural misunderstanding.
items.opening_line: I want to be honest: your comment in the meeting felt quite dismissive to me.
communicative_goals: Listen to the colleague's account without becoming defensive
Explain your intention while taking responsibility for the effect
Agree on how you will communicate with each other from now on
